survey: Wall-mounted split air-conditioner indoor unit, seen from slightly below and to the right. The white box-shaped body sits flat against the green striped wall. Its back edge touches the wall and casts a soft shadow, so it is supported. The right end has a rounded blue-grey side cap that faces the camera at an angle. The left end turns away from the viewer, so its cap is hidden, which matches the perspective. A grey trim band runs across the front, and a raised house-shaped badge sits on the upper front panel as a logo. At the bottom is the air outlet: a recessed slot with a row of evenly spaced vertical vanes and a horizontal deflector flap below it, hinged at the slot's lower lip. Blue air streams leave the outlet downward and forward, the right direction for the vanes and flap. There are no cables, pipes or other thin parts; the tools found no thin parts, ends or branches. Leaving out the refrigerant pipes and remote is a normal simplification.
